Summary: The command: Do not castrate any animal (Leviticus 22:24). No beast was to be bruised, crushed, broken, or cut, whether for offering or otherwise, in the land.
Application: This prohibition is stated generally, not only for the altar, and so it binds beyond the temple system.
Purpose: TRADITIONAL reading: mutilating an animal marred God's creation and disqualified it from the altar; the prohibition is stated generally, not only for sacrifices.
Function: No beast was to be bruised, crushed, broken, or cut, whether for offering or otherwise, in the land — a ceremonial law stated generally, not only for sacrifices. Its goal, traditionally, was to keep God's creation whole: mutilating an animal marred what God had made and disqualified it from the altar. The evil was the marring of the creature, cutting what God had formed. It restrained that by the general ban, and it was never temporary — the prohibition binds beyond the temple system.
